industry.why: Underweight, carried from last week's special topic on telecoms relative strength; neither way back to Neutral is met. Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: F now, D prior at the industry and D at the Mobile network operators sector; the United States ten-year is 'near 5%' in the one headline that gives a level (Investing Live, undated), against the 4.5% trigger; and the November results of Vodafone and Telefonica did not reach the pack. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). If the Federal Reserve easing headlines are confirmed by a dated source, this leveraged yield defensive is among the first rows to lift. To C on industry relative strength above 30 by end-January with stable churn and pricing, or the ten-year under 4.5%.

sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral, on the special topic 'The Sector Memo on telecoms relative strength: pullback or structurally impaired?', carrying the industry's letter because the 33 mobile network operators are the industry: the relative-strength uptrend is broken on every pre-set measure with 2027 estimates intact, a de-rating of a leveraged defensive in a regime that sells leverage and duration. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, D prior at the sector, F at the industry. No Pool name and no live holding; the Lists are unmoved. Counter-case: the base rate (55% of past cases back above the 200-day within 26 weeks, median +2%) is Neutral, and the ten-year under 4.5% would favour this row first. Back to C on Industry relative strength above 30 by end-January with stable churn and pricing at Vodafone and Telefonica, or the ten-year under 4.5%; to F on a lower low or churn attributed to satellites or switching tools.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Germany this week (a source pack is present, 2026-W43, and it carried nothing country-specific here), relative strength is not graded by country, and Richard's view is G10 and Europe-wide with no country line. An absence is an absence; no tilt.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
